concepts.name: Why DRAM Is Slow
facts: DRAM is slow due to weak storage signals, time-consuming sensing, destructive reads, and large dense arrays; the solution is multi-bank, multi-rank DRAM.

Weak storage signal: DRAM stores bits as tiny capacitor charges, producing only a small voltage difference on long bitlines. Sensing takes time: the sense amplifier must detect and amplify a very small voltage change into a full 0/1 value. Destructive read: reading disturbs the stored charge, so data must be restored after every row activation. Large dense arrays: DRAM prioritizes capacity and cost per bit, so rows/bitlines are long with higher RC delay. Solution: Multi-Bank, Multi-Rank DRAM.

Sensing takes time to amplify small voltage changes
Destructive read requires restore after every row activation
Large dense arrays have higher RC delay
Solution: multi-bank, multi-rank DRAM
